newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK JEWS TO SEEK OUT NAZI WAR CRIMINAL BRUNNER.
newsitem.headline: GREEK JEWS TO SEEK OUT NAZI WAR CRIMINAL BRUNNER.

text.p: Greek Jews said on Wednesday they were determined to seek the extradition from Syria of notorious Nazi war criminal Alois Brunner, blamed for the deaths of 120,000 European Jews.

"We will make an official request with the Greek Justice ministry this week," Nissim Mais, president of the central board of the Jewish Community of Greece, told Reuters. "This man was active in Salonika, where more than 50,000 Greek Jews were murdered."
Brunner, the Austrian-born SS commander and right-hand man of Adolph Eichmann, is believed to be in Syria, a country which is on good terms with Greece, he said.
"Brunner is in Syria but we cannot ask for his extradition because Greece has waived its rights on the prosecution of World War II criminals," government spokesman Dimitris Reppas told reporters.
He said Greece transferred in 1959 its extradition rights to the then West Germany.
"Our legal experts are looking into whether this can be overcome and go directly to Syria," Mais said. "If not, then we want Greece to request Germany to act on its behalf."
Mais said the Community was prompted by news reports that Brunner was alive and well and living in Damascus for the past 38 years. He would now be 84 years old.
"We know that he is so old that he might drop dead during his arrest. But it's not the man we care about, but his actions and his ideas," he said.

The last of the Nazi criminals thought to be still alive, Brunner operated in the northern Greek city of Salonika, where almost an entire community of 60,000 Jews was sent to the gas chambers in 1943.

"We know that he was methodical in his purpose, which was to eradicate Jews from the face of the earth. His victims were people of all ages and both sexes," said Mais, whose Community now has 5,000 members nationwide.

Salonika's Jewish community dates back to the second century BC and St Paul preached at its synagogue. The city known at the turn of the century as Second Jerusalem now numbers a dwindling community of 1,000 Jews.
One month after Brunner's arrival there, cattle trains began taking Jews from Salonika to Auschwitz, deporting almost the entire Jewish population in a few months.

Brunner also served as commandant of the Drancy transit concentration camp on the outskirts of Paris. Altogether he is blamed for 120,000 deaths of Jews from Greece, the former Chechoslovakia, France and Austria.
